$comment: grimoire.config.json — the project's harness configuration. Written by /grimoire:setup, read by /orchestrate, /grimoire:logs and the guard hook.

requireHook.name: rtk hook claude
requireHook.check: command -v rtk && rtk hook check "git status" | grep -q '^rtk '
requireHook.fix: brew install rtk-ai/tap/rtk && rtk init -g, then restart the session

toolHints.tracker: GitHub Issues on lecheneetsesracines/website via the authenticated gh CLI (gh issue …, gh api)

specialists.use: putting untested code under test before changing it (unit tests run with `node --test`, visual and runtime checks with Playwright)
changes to the frontmatter shape of content/**/*.md

repos.name: website

gate.run: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test:unit && npm run build && npm run test:e2e

repos.$comment: The gate type-checks with `npm run typecheck` (`next typegen && tsc --noEmit`): next-env.d.ts is gitignored and generated, so a bare `tsc` before the build fails on a fresh clone. No timeoutMin: the whole gate runs in under a minute (44 s from a fresh clone), well inside the 40-minute backstop, and a value at or under 40 would have no effect. laneSetup gives each lane a real node_modules, an APFS clone (cp -c falls back to a plain copy elsewhere): Next 16's Turbopack refuses a symlinked node_modules ('points out of the filesystem root'), and an npm install in a lane must not touch the shared checkout. A real directory already there is kept; a stale symlink or an interrupted .partial copy is replaced. `next typegen` then writes the generated types, so a type-check in the lane works before its first build.
